name: The Middleton Oak

location.address: Middleton Place, 4300 Ashley River Road, Charleston, SC 29414 (Sundial Garden)
location.neighbourhood: Middleton Place plantation gardens, Ashley River, near Summerville

access: Paid entry (Middleton Place gardens, $28-32 adult admission, open daily 9am-5pm); stands in the Sundial Garden
transport: Roughly 25-30 minutes by car northwest of downtown Charleston along Ashley River Road; no transit stop nearby
verify_notes: First Vice President of the Live Oak Society (Louisiana Garden Club Federation register, registration #1994 per WebSearch summary of the society's site -- the register PDF fetched directly (001-500.pdf, an older tranche) does not itself list Middleton Oak, so that PDF is cited only for the Society's format/existence and for the confirmed neighbouring Charleston-area registrations; the '#1994, First VP' claim itself is corroborated independently by Charleston Magazine and by louisdallaraphotography.com describing it as 'the largest measured Southern Live Oak'). Physical dimensions, DIRECTLY QUOTED from louisdallaraphotography.com: trunk diameter 10.44 feet (girth calculated as pi x diameter = ~1000cm / 32.8 ft), height 67 feet, wood volume ~4820 cubic feet as of a 2004 measurement, described until 2012 as 'the largest tree in the eastern part of the U.S.' The tree lost a large part of its crown beginning 2008, reducing its wood volume; still alive and standing per Middleton Place's own current marketing material and recent (2020s-dated) travel blog visits. Age 900-1000 years is Charleston Magazine's own figure, directly quoted; not independently re-derived here from girth, so treat as a repeated vague-source estimate rather than a fresh derivation, per the estimate rules. In 1997 a propagated offspring (now ~26ft tall) was planted just north of the parent to help protect it, per the same source. Species is Southern Live Oak per every source; not explicitly named in the Middleton Place own materials (site returned 403 to automated fetch) but stated consistently everywhere else. Do not confuse with the Angel Oak (chs_001, already published) or the Sughrue Oak/other small private Charleston-area entries in the Live Oak Society's 001-500 PDF, which are on private residential land with no address and are not candidates.
